claims: Measles symptoms typically begin 7–14 days after exposure.
Measles symptoms include a high fever.
Measles symptoms include cough.
Measles symptoms include runny nose.
Measles symptoms include red or watery eyes.
Measles symptoms include tiny white spots (Koplik spots) inside the mouth.
A characteristic red, blotchy rash appears 3–5 days after initial measles symptoms.
The measles rash starts at the hairline.
The measles rash spreads downward.
Initial measles symptoms include the '3 Cs': cough, coryza (runny nose), and conjunctivitis (red, watery, or sore eyes).
Measles high fever often spikes to over 104°F (40°C) when the rash appears.
Koplik spots are small grayish-white spots on the inner cheeks.
Koplik spots may appear 2-3 days into measles illness.
The measles rash consists of flat red spots that may merge.
The measles rash spreads from the face/neck down to the body.
On darker skin, the measles rash may appear brown or purplish.
Measles-infected individuals can spread the virus for about 4 days before the rash appears until 4 days after.
Ear infections occur in about 1 in 10 children with measles.
Diarrhea is reported in less than 1 in 10 people with measles.
Encephalitis is swelling of the brain.
Encephalitis occurs in about 1 in 1,000 measles cases.
Encephalitis can cause permanent damage.
